card: Adds UNIX domain socket support to the HTTP RPC server and bitcoin-cli using -rpcbind=unix[:path] and -rpcconnect=unix[:path]. This enables local RPC communication without TCP loopback overhead, relying on filesystem permissions instead of -rpcallowip. The PR also refactors netbase by introducing UnixSocketAddr and SocketAddr, resolving technical debt left from PR #27375. This closes issue #5029, a feature request open since 2014.
changed_since_previous: Added release notes and documentation for JSON-RPC, and extended functional test coverage for bitcoin-cli over UNIX domain sockets in interface_bitcoin_cli.py and test_runner.py.
evidence: Closes issue #5029, an open feature request for UNIX domain socket support in RPC since 2014.
Description notes that earlier UNIX socket support in #27375 created technical debt in Proxy that this PR resolves with generic abstractions.
problem: Local JSON-RPC and REST communication previously required TCP loopback connections, forcing node operators to manage IP-based allowlists instead of operating system filesystem permissions and incurring TCP stack overhead. Additionally, earlier UNIX socket support added in PR #27375 was isolated to the Proxy class, leaving technical debt where socket abstractions were tangled with P2P networking classes.

risk.why: A mistake in socket path resolution or socket binding permissions could prevent local RPC access or inadvertently expose the RPC interface to unauthorized local users.

scope_notes: Refactors networking abstractions across netbase and httpserver by replacing CService with SocketAddr (a std::variant of CService and UnixSocketAddr) in HTTPRemoteClient and Proxy. Includes substantial new unit tests in src/test/netbase_tests.cpp (+498 lines) and functional test framework support via --httpunix.
summary: Adds UNIX domain socket support to Bitcoin Core's HTTP RPC server and bitcoin-cli via the -rpcbind and -rpcconnect configuration options using unix and unix:<path> syntax. It introduces UnixSocketAddr and a SocketAddr variant in netbase to decouple generic endpoint handling from P2P-specific networking classes like CService, and updates Proxy and HTTPServer accordingly. When binding exclusively to UNIX domain sockets, -rpcallowip is no longer required and default TCP loopback listeners are disabled.
